notes: Read all 74 source lines line by line before editing. This is a non-visual data/config module, so per contract rule 6 the logic/types were ported faithfully into native-compatible TypeScript.

Source lines 1-2 (`import type { TourDefinition } from '@/lib/tourRegistry'` and `import type { TourStep } from '@/hooks/useTour'`) are erased compile-time-only type imports. Source lines 4-10 (the JSDoc block describing the dashboard auto-start tour and the version-bump invalidation behavior) are preserved verbatim above the STEPS const.

Source lines 12-62 (the STEPS: TourStep[] array of 7 steps) are preserved exactly — every target selector ([data-tour="sidebar"|"dashboard-grid"|"edit-mode-btn"|"vehicle-section"|"commands-section"|"live-signals-section"|"keyboard-hint"]), every title, every description string (including em-dashes, the '70+'/'230+' figures, and the apostrophe in "don't" kept in double quotes per prettier avoidEscape on L31), and every placement ('right'/'bottom'/'top') are byte-identical.

Source lines 64-74 (export const MAIN_TOUR: TourDefinition) are preserved exactly: id 'main', routeMatch '/', titleKey 'tour.tours.main.title', titleFallback 'Welcome to TeslaSync', descriptionKey 'tour.tours.main.description', descriptionFallback 'A quick tour of the dashboard, sidebar, and live data.', version 2, steps: STEPS, and the autoStart predicate `({pathname, vehicleCount}) => pathname === '/' && vehicleCount > 0` — i18n keys/fallbacks and the route-match behavior are unchanged.

No DOM-only modules, browser HTML elements, Recharts, Leaflet, or web UI components are imported; the file is pure TypeScript with zero runtime imports and is therefore native-safe. No units or numeric conversions exist in this module, so unit handling is preserved trivially.

Native-runtime note (contract rule 7): `TourStep.target` values are DOM-selector strings and `placement` is tooltip-relative-to-DOM positioning; React Native has no querySelector/DOMRect. These are preserved here as opaque tour-definition data (no DOM access happens in this data file) so the eventual native tour runtime (the future port of useTour/tourRegistry) can map selectors to view refs/anchors. The data contract is intact; only the consuming runtime will differ.
